extracted.intended_audience: PCT applicants, patent agents/attorneys, and national/intergovernmental patent Offices (receiving Offices, International Searching Authorities, Authorities specified for supplementary search, International Preliminary Examining Authorities, International Bureau)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules governing filing, processing, communications, agents, withdrawals, time limits (excuse and extension), electronic filing, Gazette publication, amendments, and rectification of mistakes under the Patent Cooperation Treaty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excuse of Delay in Meeting Time Limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Any interested party may offer evidence that a time limit fixed in the Regulations for performing an action before the receiving Office, the International Searching Authority, the Authority specified for supplementary search, the International Preliminary Examining Authority or the International Bureau was not met due to war, revolution, civil disorder, strike, natural calamity, epidemic, a general unavailability of electronic communications services or other like reason in the locality where the interested party resides, has his place of business or is staying, and that the relevant action was taken as soon as reasonably possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such evidence must be addressed to the Office, Authority or the International Bureau not later than six months after the expiration of the time limit. If circumstances are proven to the satisfaction of the addressee, delay shall be excused. The excuse need not be taken into account by any designated or elected Office before which the applicant has already performed the acts referred to in Article 22 or Article 39 at the time the decision to excuse the delay is taken. The need for evidence may be waived by the Office/Authority/International Bureau under published conditions; in that case the interested party must submit a statement that failure to meet the time limit was due to the waived reason and the Office/Authority shall notify the International Bureau.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unavailability of Electronic Means of Communication at the Office
rubrics_metrics.description: A national Office or intergovernmental organization may provide that, where a time limit fixed in the Regulations for performing an action before that Office or organization is not met due to the unavailability of any of the permitted electronic means of communication at that Office or organization, delay in meeting that time limit shall be excused, provided that the respective action was performed on the next working day on which the said electronic means of communication were available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office/organization must publish information on any such unavailability including the period and notify the International Bureau. The excuse of delay under this provision need not be taken into account by any designated or elected Office before which the applicant has already performed the acts referred to in Article 22 or Article 39 at the time the information is published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of Time Limits due to General Disruption
rubrics_metrics.description: Any receiving Office, International Searching Authority, Authority specified for supplementary search, International Preliminary Examining Authority or the International Bureau may establish a period of extension such that time limits fixed in the Regulations within which a party has to perform an action before that Office/Authority/International Bureau may be extended when the State in which it is located is experiencing a general disruption caused by an event listed in Rule 82quater.1(a) which affects operations and interferes with the ability of parties to perform actions within the time limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office/Authority/International Bureau shall publish the commencement and end date of any such period; the period shall not be longer than two months from the date of commencement, and additional periods may be established if necessary. Extensions need not be taken into account by any designated or elected Office if, at the time the information is published, national processing before that Office has started.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of Right to Practice before International Authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau, the competent International Searching Authority, and the competent International Preliminary Examining Authority may require the production of proof of the right to practice referred to in Article 49.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This empowers those bodies to request documentary proof of entitlement to represent applicants before the respective international authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where the International Bureau Is the Receiving Office — Entitlement to Practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who has the right to practice before the national Office of, or acting for, a Contracting State of which the applicant (or any of multiple applicants) is a resident or national shall be entitled to practice in respect of the international application before the International Bureau in its capacity as receiving Office under Rule 19.1(a)(iii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any person having the right to practice before the International Bureau as receiving Office shall be entitled to practice before the International Bureau in any other capacity and before the competent ISA and competent IPEA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information on Right to Practice Binding
rubrics_metrics.description: The national Office or intergovernmental organization which the interested person is alleged to have a right to practice before shall, upon request, inform the International Bureau, the competent ISA, or the competent IPEA whether such person has the right to practice before it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such information shall be binding upon the International Bureau, the ISA, or the IPEA, as the case may be.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gazette — Required Contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The Gazette shall contain, for example, the schedule of all fees payable to the receiving Offices, the International Bureau, and the International Searching and Preliminary Examining Authorities; notices the publication of which is required under the Treaty or Regulations; information concerning events at the designated and elected Offices notified to the International Bureau in relation to published international applications; and any other useful information prescribed by the Administrative Instructions, provided access to such information is not prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each published international application, the information referred to in Rule 86.1(i) is to be published in the Gazette on, or as soon as possible after, the date of publication of the international application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gazette — Languages, Form, Timing, Frequency and Sale
rubrics_metrics.description: The Gazette shall be published in English and French at the same time (translations ensured by the International Bureau); the Assembly may order publication in other languages; the form and means of publication are governed by the Administrative Instructions; the frequency is determined by the Director General.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Gazette referred to in Article 55(4) shall contain for each published international application the data specified by the Administrative Instructions taken from the front page, the drawing (if any) appearing on said front page, and the abstract. Subscription and sale prices and the title of the Gazette are determined by the Director General; further details may be provided in the Administrative Instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication of Publications on Request
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau shall communicate, free of charge, every published international application, the Gazette and any other publication of general interest published by the International Bureau in connection with the Treaty or these Regulations, to ISAs, IPEAs and national Offices upon request by the Authority or Office concerned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further details concerning the form and means by which publications are communicated shall be governed by the Administrative Instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of the Regulations — Unanimity and Procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendment of certain specified provisions of the Regulations shall require that no State having the right to vote in the Assembly vote against the proposed amendment (Rule 88.1 lists such provisions). Amendments of other specified provisions require that no State referred to in Article 58(3)(a)(ii) and having the right to vote vote against (Rule 88.3 lists those provisions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any proposal for amending such provisions to be decided in the Assembly shall be communicated to all Contracting States at least two months prior to the opening of that session of the Assembly called to decide on the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Instructions — Scope and Non-Conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrative Instructions shall contain provisions concerning matters expressly referred to in the Regulations and any details in respect of the application of the Regulations, but shall not be in conflict with the Treaty, these Regulations, or any agreement concluded by the International Bureau with an ISA or an IPEA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative Instructions are drawn up and promulgated by the Director General after consultation with receiving Offices and ISAs/IPEAs, may be modified after consultation, the Assembly may invite modification, and they are published in the Gazette specifying effective dates (which may vary by provision).

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic Filing of International Applications — General Rule
rubrics_metrics.description: International applications may, subject to Administrative Instructions, be filed and processed in electronic form or by electronic means, provided that any receiving Office shall permit the filing of international applications on paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Regulations apply mutatis mutandis to electronic applications, subject to special provisions in the Administrative Instructions. The Administrative Instructions set out requirements regarding acknowledgment of receipt, according of an international filing date, physical requirements, consequences of non-compliance, signature of documents, authentication of documents and party identity, operation of Article 12 re home/record/search copies, and may differ by language. No national Office/organization is obliged to receive/process electronic filings unless it has notified the International Bureau that it is prepared to do so in compliance with Administrative Instructions; the IB shall publish such notifications. A receiving Office that notified the IB may not refuse to process an electronic filing which complies with the Administrative Instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic Filing and Communication of Other Documents; Inter-Office Electronic Communications; Electronic Copies of Paper Filings
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions on electronic international applications apply mutatis mutandis to other correspondence and documents relating to international applications. Communication by one national Office or intergovernmental organization to another may, where agreed by both sender and receiver, be effected in electronic form or by electronic means. Any national Office or intergovernmental organization may provide that a copy in electronic form of a paper-filed international application or other document, in accordance with the Administrative Instructions, may be furnished by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These provisions require mutual agreement for electronic transmittal between Offices and permit Offices to accept electronic copies of paper filings according to Administrative Instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of Agent (Right to Practice Requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person having the right to practice before the national Office with which the international application is filed or, where filed with the International Bureau, having the right to practice in respect of the international application before the International Bureau as receiving Office may be appointed by the applicant as his agent to represent him before the receiving Office, the International Bureau, the ISA, any Authority specified for supplementary search and the IPEA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific provisions allow appointment of persons who have the right to practice before the Office/Authority acting as ISA, supplementary search Authority or IPEA to represent the applicant before those Authorities. An agent may appoint sub-agents provided the sub-agent has the right to practice before the relevant Office; conditions and limitations on appointment are detailed in Rule 90.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common Representative — Appointment and Default
rubrics_metrics.description: Where there are two or more applicants and the applicants have not appointed an agent representing all (a common agent), one of the applicants entitled to file may be appointed by the others as their common representative. If applicants have not appointed a common agent or common representative, the applicant first named in the request who is entitled to file shall be considered the common representative of all applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acts by or in relation to a common representative or his agent shall have the effect of acts by or in relation to all the applicants (subject to certain exceptions in Rule 90 bis.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of Acts by Agents and Multiple Agents
rubrics_metrics.description: Any act by or in relation to an agent shall have the effect of an act by or in relation to the applicant(s). If there are two or more agents representing the same applicant(s), any act by or in relation to any of those agents shall have the effect of an act by or in relation to the applicant(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subject to Rule 90 bis.5 second sentence, any act by or in relation to a common representative or his agent shall have the effect of an act by or in relation to all the applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner of Appointment and Power of Attorney Formalities
rubrics_metrics.description: The appointment of an agent is effected by the applicant signing the request, the demand or a separate power of attorney; where two or more applicants, each signs the request/demand or separate power. A separate power of attorney shall be submitted to the receiving Office or the International Bureau (and when appointing agents for specific Authorities it must be submitted to those Authorities). If the separate power of attorney is not signed or required information is missing or does not comply with Rule 4.4, it is considered non-existent unless corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offices/Authorities may waive the requirement to submit a separate power of attorney; however, where agent/common representative submits a notice of withdrawal (Rules 90 bis.1-90 bis.4), the waiver shall not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Power of Attorney (GPOA) — Deposit and Use
rubrics_metrics.description: Appointment of an agent in relation to a particular international application may be effected by referring in the request/demand/separate notice to an existing separate power of attorney appointing that agent to represent the applicant in relation to any international application (a 'general power of attorney'), provided the GPOA has been deposited and a copy of it is attached to the request/demand/separate notice (copy need not be signed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The general power of attorney shall be deposited with the receiving Office (or with the ISA/supplementary Authority/IPEA where it appoints agents before those Authorities). Offices/Authorities may waive the requirement that a copy of the GPOA is attached; notwithstanding waiver, where the agent submits a notice of withdrawal under Rules 90 bis.1 to 90 bis.4 to the receiving Office/Authority/Bureau, a copy of the GPOA shall be submitted to that Office/Authority/Bureau.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation and Renunciation of Appointment
rubrics_metrics.description: Any appointment of an agent or common representative may be revoked by the persons who made the appointment or their successors in title; any appointment of a sub-agent by that agent is also considered revoked. An agent or common representative may renounce his appointment by a notification signed by him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appointment of an agent under Rule 90.1(a) shall, unless otherwise indicated, have the effect of revoking any earlier appointment under that Rule. Rule 90.4(b) and (c) apply mutatis mutandis to documents containing revocations or renunciations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of the International Application
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may withdraw the international application at any time prior to the expiration of 30 months from the priority date. Withdrawal is effective on receipt of a notice addressed by the applicant, at his option, to the International Bureau, to the receiving Office or, where Article 39(1) applies, to the IPEA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No international publication shall be effected if the notice of withdrawal reaches the International Bureau before the technical preparations for international publication have been completed. Withdrawal of designations follows similar timing and effect rules; withdrawal of the designations of all designated States shall be treated as withdrawal of the international application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of Priority Claims and Effect on Time Limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may withdraw a priority claim made in the international application under Article 8(1) at any time prior to the expiration of 30 months from the priority date. Where the international application contains more than one priority claim, the applicant may withdraw one or more or all of the priority claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawal is effective on receipt of notice to the IB/RO/IPEA. Where withdrawal causes a change in the priority date, any time limit computed from the original priority date and which has not already expired shall, subject to paragraph (e), be computed from the resulting priority date. For Article 21(2)(a) the IB may nevertheless proceed with publication on the basis of the original priority-date-computed time limit if the notice reaches the IB after technical preparations for publication have been completed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of Supplementary Search Request
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may withdraw a supplementary search request at any time prior to the date of transmittal to the applicant and to the International Bureau of the supplementary international search report or the declaration that no such report will be established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawal shall be effective on receipt within that time limit of a notice by the applicant to the Authority specified for supplementary search or to the International Bureau; however, if the notice does not reach the Authority in sufficient time to prevent transmittal, the transmittal of the report or declaration may nevertheless be effected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of the Demand or of Elections
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may withdraw the demand or any or all elections at any time prior to the expiration of 30 months from the priority date. Withdrawal shall be effective upon receipt of a notice addressed by the applicant to the International Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the notice is submitted to the IPEA, that Authority shall mark the date of receipt on the notice and transmit it promptly to the International Bureau; the notice shall be considered to have been submitted to the International Bureau on the date marked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature Requirement for Withdrawal Notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Any notice of withdrawal referred to in Rules 90 bis.1 to 90 bis.4 shall be signed by the applicant or, if there are two or more applicants, by all of them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An applicant considered to be the common representative under Rule 90.2(b) shall not be entitled to sign such a notice on behalf of the other applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Withdrawal on National Processing and International Processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Withdrawal under Rule 90 bis of the international application, any designation, any priority claim, the demand or any election shall have no effect in any designated or elected Office where the processing or examination of the international application has already started under Article 23(2) or Article 40(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the international application is withdrawn under Rule 90 bis.1, the international processing shall be discontinued. Withdrawal of a supplementary search request discontinues that supplementary international search. Withdrawal of the demand or all elections discontinues processing by the IPEA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification under Article 37(4)(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Contracting State whose national law provides for what is described in the second part of Article 37(4)(b) shall notify the International Bureau in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notification shall be promptly published by the International Bureau in the Gazette, and shall have effect in respect of international applications filed more than one month after the date of such publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rectification of Obvious Mistakes — Authorization Test and Competent Authority
rubrics_metrics.description: An obvious mistake in the international application or another document submitted by the applicant may be rectified if the applicant requests. The rectification is subject to authorization by the 'competent authority' defined by the subject-matter of the mistake: (i) mistake in the request part — receiving Office; (ii) mistake in the description, claims or drawings or correction thereof — International Searching Authority (unless IPEA is competent under (iii)); (iii) where a demand for international preliminary examination has been made and not withdrawn and the date on which international preliminary examination shall start has passed — International Preliminary Examining Authority; (iv) mistake in other documents submitted to RO/ISA/IPEA/IB (other than abstract or Article 19 amendment) — that Office/Authority/Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The competent authority shall authorize rectification if, and only if, it is obvious to that authority that, as at the applicable date, something else was intended than what appears and that nothing else could have been intended than the proposed rectification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rectification — Evidence to be Considered and Applicable Date
rubrics_metrics.description: For mistakes in description/claims/drawings the competent authority shall, for purposes of determining obviousness, take into account only the contents of the description, claims and drawings and any applicable correction/amendment. For mistakes in the request part or other documents, the authority shall take into account the contents of the international application itself and any submitted corrections, accompanying documents, any available priority document, and any other document in the authority’s international application file at the applicable date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicable date is: (i) the international filing date for a mistake in a part of the international application as filed; (ii) the date on which the document was submitted for mistakes in a document other than the international application as filed (including corrections/amendments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-rectifiable Mistakes and Invitation to Request Rectification
rubrics_metrics.description: A mistake shall not be rectifiable if: (i) the mistake lies in the omission of one or more entire elements of the international application referred to in Article 3(2) or one or more entire sheets; (ii) the mistake is in the abstract; (iii) the mistake is in an amendment under Article 19, unless the IPEA is competent; or (iv) the mistake is in a priority claim or in a notice correcting/adding a priority claim under Rule 26 bis.1(a) where rectification would cause a change in the priority date (subject to operation of other Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where an Office/Authority/IB discovers what appears to be a rectifiable obvious mistake, it may invite the applicant to request rectification under this Rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Rectification — Content and Time Limit
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for rectification must be submitted to the competent authority within 26 months from the priority date. It shall specify the mistake to be rectified and the proposed rectification and may contain a brief explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 26.4 applies mutatis mutandis as to the manner in which the proposed rectification shall be indicated.
